source: priced from each configuration's parts against a token's GPU-seconds at serving's MFU on the H200's dense FP8 peak (total_cost.priced_card); measured values replace it configuration by configuration

value.baseline: stock vLLM, compiled, on the model's served circuit

parts.source: throughput 0.984 of vLLM's on the mean run and 0.96 on the worst, a queue-dependent tick on Llama-3.2-1B traces, simulated and validated against them; on GLM-5.3 at TP8, with certified arrivals and prefix caching off, it leaves no scheduling advice but the response length, which stays advice until a circuit checks the stop rule; the run with the real network certifier is pending (a client stood in for it in the measured runs, which served with prefix caching on)

the scheduler's record of each step, written on the engine core's thread: 98 µs a step, timed on the serving path's writer off the engine, over the step of one engine across eight H200s under the chat load at 384 requests at once (147 ms a step, 143 rows a step, 4.9 requests finished a second, measured on stock compiled vLLM), as if it lengthened every step; the high at a full batch of 256 rows, 173 µs; the low 0, vLLM's queue of two batches letting the thread write while the cards run; with the record on, GLM-5.3's throughput at TP8 was measured within noise of stock compiled vLLM's at every load

its hooks on the engine core's thread, 11.2 µs a step and 4.4 µs a request admitted, timed off the engine, on one engine across eight H200s under the chat load at 384 requests at once (147 ms a step, 143 rows a step, 4.9 requests finished a second, measured on stock compiled vLLM), as if they lengthened every step; the high adds its commit thread's rows, salts, hashes and files, 0.41 to 1.09 ms a finished request, as if each second of that thread, which shares the engine core's interpreter, were taken from serving; the low 0; priced with each size class's replay block's program digested once: a commit thread that builds the program again for every window and class costs more, and that is not in this part

2,061 B a token hashed at the commitment card's rate, the range at 446 and 289 GB/s; one attention layer's table for each request, 1,472 B hashed on the card a row (the row's 1,152 B, its 192 B salt and the tree node above its leaf) at 1.4 rows a computed token on the chat load's size classes, 1 to 2 over the range; the hashing alone, without the rows' gather from the layer's state and their copy to the host; no served run has built a table
